title: U.S. House · Texas's 33rd District
area: A Dallas-Fort Worth-area district covering parts of Dallas and Tarrant counties.

context.text: Texas redrew its congressional map for the 2026 election cycle. Under the new lines, Colin Allred (who previously represented the old 32nd District and ran for U.S. Senate in 2024) defeated incumbent Rep. Julie Johnson in the Democratic primary runoff for this seat. Rep. Marc Veasey, who previously represented a Fort Worth-area district, did not make the general-election ballot for this district. Patrick Gillespie defeated John Sims in the Republican primary runoff. Michelle Craig is running as a declared independent write-in candidate.

candidates.name: Colin Allred
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Democratic primary runoff, defeating incumbent Rep. Julie Johnson
candidates.currentRole: Former U.S. Representative (TX-32, 2019-2025); civil rights attorney

summary.text: Colin Allred is a former NFL linebacker and civil rights attorney who represented the old Texas 32nd District as a Democrat from 2019 to 2025. He left the House to run for U.S. Senate in 2024, losing to Ted Cruz, then re-filed in 2026 for the redrawn 33rd District after ending a second Senate campaign. He defeated incumbent Rep. Julie Johnson in the May 26, 2026 Democratic runoff.

background.text: Born April 15, 1983, in Dallas, Texas, and raised by his mother, a public school teacher; graduated from Hillcrest High School in Dallas.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Baylor University in 2005, where he played linebacker on the football team.
Signed with the Tennessee Titans as an undrafted free agent in 2006 and played linebacker in the NFL until a neck injury in 2010 ended his career.
Earned a J.D. from the University of California, Berkeley School of Law in 2014.

After law school, worked for Battleground Texas as Dallas-Fort Worth regional director of voter protection, served as a special assistant in the Obama administration's Department of Housing and Urban Development, and later worked as a civil rights and voting-rights litigator at the law firm Perkins Coie.

Won the Democratic nomination in 2018 and defeated Republican incumbent Pete Sessions in the general election for the 32nd District; re-elected in 2020 and 2022, serving from January 3, 2019, to January 3, 2025.
In Congress, served on the Foreign Affairs and Transportation and Infrastructure committees, and on Veterans' Affairs in the 116th and 117th Congresses, according to Ballotpedia.
Ran for U.S. Senate in 2024 rather than seeking re-election, winning the Democratic nomination and losing the general election to Ted Cruz, 53.1% to 44.6%.

Announced a 2026 Senate campaign in July 2025 and ended it in December 2025 to run for the 33rd District; won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 45.5% and the May 26 runoff over Rep. Julie Johnson, 54.0% to 46.0%.

priorities.text: Says he delivered more than $135 million in federal funding for public transportation, health care, affordable housing and law enforcement within the district while in Congress, and led the effort to open a new VA hospital in Garland.
Says he will fight to protect the Affordable Care Act and expand access to affordable health care.
Supports investments in child care, early childhood education, and job and skills training.
priorities.quote: Through smart investments in affordable child care, early childhood education, job and skills training and expanding health care coverage we can increase productivity and grow our economy in a way that works for everyone.

positions.summary: Says he will fight to protect access to abortion.
positions.quote: I will fight to protect the freedom to access the health care you need, including access to an abortion.

positions.summary: Says he supports background checks on all gun sales and red-flag laws.
positions.quote: support common sense approaches to reducing gun violence such as criminal background checks on all gun sales

positions.summary: Says he supports protecting and expanding the Affordable Care Act and access to affordable health care.
Supports investments in affordable child care and early childhood education.
Calls for abolishing ICE and moving its functions to other agencies, and for ending indefinite detention.
positions.quote: Colin will fight to abolish ICE and build a just immigration system in Congress

positions.summary: Calls for repealing the Trump tariffs, with targeted exceptions for national security.
positions.quote: Repeal Trump's tariffs with targeted exceptions for national security and reassert the constitutional authority of Congress over trade policy

positions.summary: Calls for requiring the wealthiest Americans to pay into Social Security at the same rate as everyone else.
positions.quote: require the wealthiest Americans to pay in at the same rate as everyone else

positions.summary: Calls for reversing the Trump administration's cuts to renewable power.
positions.quote: Reverse Trump's cuts to renewable power and eliminate costly energy tariffs

record.text: Named the most bipartisan member of the Texas congressional delegation during his House service, according to his campaign; was a member of the Bipartisan Paid Leave Working Group and took paternity leave after the births of his sons.

candidates.name: Patrick Gillespie
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Republican primary runoff against John Sims
candidates.currentRole: Technical writer; former labor union local vice president

summary.text: Patrick Gillespie is the Republican nominee, a technical writer and former union local officer originally from West Virginia who has lived in Texas since 1984. He has not held elected office; he was the Republican nominee against Rep. Marc Veasey in 2022 and 2024 and won the 2026 Republican runoff over John Sims. In his Ballotpedia survey responses, he lists border security among his priorities.

background.text: Born in Huntington, West Virginia, in 1957, according to his Ballotpedia survey; graduated from Huntington High School and attended Marshall University.

Worked as a technical writer at Boeing, BAE Systems, American Airlines and Flextronics International; in his survey he put his tenure at about 19.5 years at Boeing, 8 years at BAE Systems and 10 years at American Airlines.
In his survey, described working at UPS Supply Chain Solutions in its international division and doing part-time parts inspection for Lockheed Martin.
Served as vice president of Local Lodge 2768 of the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers.
Was the Republican nominee for the 33rd District in 2022, losing to Rep. Marc Veasey 72.0% to 25.6%, and again in 2024, losing 68.8% to 31.2%.
Won the May 26, 2026 Republican primary runoff over John Sims, 57.1% to 42.9%, to become the nominee for the redrawn district.

priorities.text: Calls for stronger enforcement of existing immigration law and opposes what he describes as an "invasion" at the southern border.
Supports getting the U.S. out of the Paris Climate Accords and expanding domestic natural-gas electricity generation instead of coal.
Calls for balancing the federal budget and paying down the national debt.
priorities.quote: 32 TRILLION DOLLARS INDEBT! Stop spending money we don’t have! Balance the budget and pay down the debt with any surplus.

positions.summary: Opposes U.S. participation in the Paris Climate Accords and favors switching coal-fired electricity generation to natural gas rather than mandating faster transition away from fossil fuels.
positions.quote: The U.S. can switch to natural gas for all the electric generation done by coal in the U.S. Plus, get out of the Paris Climate Accords and demand our money back.

statements.quote: Red flag laws are proving not to be a deterrent to gun violence. I would advocate those laws on the books be enforced. I will not propose the abolition of the 2nd Amendment.
statements.context: On his campaign website, answering a question about curbing gun violence

statements.quote: 25+ MILLION ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS! Enforce the laws on the books!!
statements.context: On his campaign website, answering a question about the most important challenges facing the country

candidates.name: Michelle Craig
candidates.ballotNote: Running as a declared write-in candidate

summary.text: Michelle Craig is an independent write-in candidate for the 33rd District. In her Ballotpedia survey she describes herself as a Texas native running as an independent, and little other biographical information is public.

background.text: Describes herself in a Ballotpedia survey as born in Texas and having lived most of her life in the state.
Is running as a declared independent write-in candidate in the November 3, 2026 general election; Ballotpedia lists no prior offices or professional history for her.

researchNotes: No 2026-specific Candidate Connection survey exists for Allred or Gillespie; Allred's positions rely on Ballotpedia-quoted campaign-website text; Gillespie's rely on his Ballotpedia survey and his own campaign website (patrickgillespie4congress33.com, read directly). Gillespie's site uses a photo-ID answer on ballot access, which is not recorded under proof of citizenship. No public biography, platform, or survey responses were found for write-in candidate Michelle Craig, so her entry is minimal. Write-in candidate Michelle Craig completed a 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey but gives little biographical detail, and no news coverage or campaign biography was found, so her entry is minimal. Allred's biography relies on Ballotpedia, Wikipedia and Ballotpedia News because his congressional pages and a current campaign biography could not be loaded; Gillespie's employment details come from his own survey responses.
